component_findings.current_continuity: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-2--rust): A community-maintained roster of companies attributes specific production use cases directly to company statements, e.g. AWS and Atlassian.
component_findings.deployment_depth: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-2--rust): Rust scores very high (92/100): production deployment evidence is unusually strong and diverse for a systems language of Rust's age, spanning multiple hyperscalers (AWS, Microsoft, Google), a dedicated Foundation-run commercial coordination body with those same companies as founding members, and named case studies (Cloudflare, Discord, Atlassian). Score is not maximal because independent reporting confirms adoption is still predominantly incremental/component-level rather than wholesale replacement of legacy systems, and some cited statistics originate from secondary blog aggregation rather than primary company disclosures.

metric.production_adoption_deployment_ev.limitations: Some adoption figures come from marketing-oriented blog aggregations (e.g. 'X% growth' style posts) with unclear original methodology and are treated as lower-confidence corroborating context rather than primary evidence; the primary basis for the score is the combination of named, verifiable hyperscaler production systems (Firecracker, Windows, Android) and the Rust Foundation's own formally documented Commercial Network membership.
metric.production_adoption_deployment_ev.selection_rule: Use public, independently checkable production evidence; named deployments must be documented by the deploying organization or corroborated by credible independent sources. Popularity surveys alone do not prove deployment.

component_findings.build_test_coverage: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-2--rust): <cite index="11-11,11-12,11-13,11-14,11-15,11-16,11-17">Every mature Rust project should cover all three layers. Layer 1: Linting and style catches idiomatic violations, common mistakes, and maintainability problems. Tools: Clippy, rustfmt, rust-analyzer. Layer 3: Deep verification finds memory safety issues in unsafe code, undefined behavior, and formally proves properties of critical functions. Tools: Miri, Kani, MIRAI, Rudra, Creusot, Prusti.</cite>

component_findings.editor_ide: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-2--rust): Rust scores very high (91/100): it has an officially endorsed, first-party IDE protocol (rust-analyzer) plus an independent commercial IDE (RustRover), official compiler-adjacent linter/formatter (Clippy/rustfmt), a mature layered third-party security/verification tool stack (cargo-audit, cargo-deny, Miri, Kani et al.), and first-party SDKs from both major cloud vendors (AWS, Azure). The score is not 100 because some tooling (e.g., RustRover) is proprietary/commercial-licensed for non-hobby use, and some verification tools (Kani, Prusti, Creusot) remain research-grade/niche rather than mainstream-production-hardened.
component_findings.lint_format_static: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-2--rust): A recognized layered third-party static-analysis stack exists beyond the compiler: style/lint (Clippy, rustfmt, rust-analyzer), supply-chain security (cargo-audit, cargo-deny, cargo-auditable), and deep verification (Miri, Kani, MIRAI, Rudra, Creusot, Prusti).

metric.third_party_tool_availability.limitations: Crate/download counts on lib.rs and GitHub star/plugin counts were consulted only as supplementary context and are not used as the sole basis for the score; the qualitative official-recommendation and named-tool findings above are the primary basis. Only one retrieval route (web search against official/vendor pages) was used, consistent with parity across languages in this shard.
metric.third_party_tool_availability.selection_rule: Inspect the same fixed tool categories for every language and require independently maintained current tools; official first-party tools may be cited only as context, not as third-party availability.
